issue.title: TUI GC policy still permits 32-second main-thread collections and recurrent multi-second hitches
issue.description: Observed after closed epic sase-1ez (2026-10-03). GCPolicy.tick calls collector.collect synchronously; the telemetry provides direct stop duration, while the exact producer of the large cyclic graph remains unproven. Plan a bounded allocation/object-retention investigation across fleet projection and recurring snapshots, compare Python 3.14.7 athena versus 3.12.3 apollo, and preserve memory backstops. Do not merely raise thresholds or move CPython GC to a worker and assume it cannot pause the process. Measure by app instance and revision, compare matched retained intervals and prompt-active/idle behavior, and validate a long-lived representative roster. Large because cause attribution and a measured performance fix require planning; link to closed sase-1ez and related active sase-zn without claiming the latter caused this regression.

task_type_fields.impact: Long-lived TUI processes remain visibly frozen for seconds despite the installed GC policy; idle gating does not bound a collection after input resumes.
task_type_fields.repro: Athena 2026-10-20 epoch 1792496103.287799: tui_gc_pause generation=2 duration_s=32.44874 thread=MainThread trigger=backstop collected=590483, app_instance_id=d2b7cd41 (tui_stalls.jsonl.1 line 1876 in audit snapshot). Related hitch duration=36.954 with gc_overlap_s=33.138 at epoch 1792496105.2534344. A later idle collection took 23.506427s and collected 649759 objects. Retained first sweep counted 329 recovered loop hitches on athena and 185 on apollo, across different retention windows.

evidence.note: Still reproduces on fixed code (from sase-1nf.14.1 phases .7/.8 PROPOSED FOLLOW-UPs, triaged by the sase-1nf.14.1 land agent). Source 196690f6cb with SASE_TUI_PERF=1 and SASE_TUI_GC_CENSUS=1, instances Athena 8b65de59 (Py 3.14.7) and Apollo 7e973b00 (Py 3.12.3). Over ~7,229 s post-warmup (not 4 h or 24 h), idle full-GC p95 was 4.476/1.051 s (limit 0.5), GC share 12.60%/4.28% (limit 3%), and loop-hitch share 15.29%/0.71% (limit 0.5%). Athena VmSwap max was 631,345,152 B. Contiguous fragments also fail. Census time is included, not subtracted. Not a controlled before/after against r5: workload, host load (Athena load1 up to 119), and roster all differ. CAVEAT: this measured code LACKS the graph-allocation fix (sase-1nf.14.1.3, the top-ranked producer). That phase's commit was lost when its agent crashed and a workspace lease reset discarded the changes. The diff was recovered as file:explicit:cc1fcd3f9d4bd944a9c454b5 and is being re-landed by the sase-1nf.14.1 closeout. Re-measure after it lands.

payload.entry: Sequencing handoff from epic sase-1q5 (TUI index-lock starvation fix, proposed by phase sase-1q5.8). (1) Re-run this track's soak on a restarted TUI now that sase-1q5 has landed. Earlier soak failures, including the 2026-10-30 +1 from sase-1nf.14.1.land, measured the O(archive) fallback-scan load regression that sase-1q5 removed. Follow docs/contribute/perf-runbook.md 'Re-measure after the index-lock fix'. tools/tui_freeze_report now reports slow agent loads by index-stage bucket and artifact_source/repair_reason. (2) Run the one-time SASE_TUI_GC_CENSUS=1 census on that restarted instance to attribute the residual 8M to 19M block growth before any retention work. (3) Research Step 4 stays evidence-gated on that remeasure: a reader/writer split of the artifact-index lock, an immutable versioned Agents read model, and the JSON name-registry retention gap. Open those only if the restarted measurement still shows index-lock contention or retention growth. GC decision rule: only if idle gen-2 p95 still exceeds 0.5 s, adopt the long-quiet, cost-gated gen-2 policy. Never lower threshold2, disable GC, or move collection to a worker.
